study: Phase 3: single confirmatory test of BTC 30-day time-series momentum (Phase 2.1 hypothesis H1)

relation_to_phase2_1.what: A NEW study. Under the Phase 2.1 pre-registration H1 failed the training gate (raw timing p 0.028, Holm-adjusted 0.140) and that study forbids looking at validation for train failures. This study is the separately registered single-hypothesis confirmation proposed in RESEARCH_HYPOTHESES.md section 5 and authorised by the owner.
identical_to_phase2_1: timing test (code path, shift count, minimum shift, seed)
relation_to_phase2_1.selection_disclosure: H1 was chosen as the best of 5 hypotheses on the TRAINING segment only. No validation or hold-out row of binance-2020 has been evaluated for any hypothesis before this registration. About 850 BTCUSDT configurations were examined in Phase 1 on different data (2025-26).

naming_note: 'H1' is the hypothesis identifier. Bars are DAILY, not hourly.

hypothesis.rule: exposure 1 if trailing 30-day log return of the daily close > 0 else 0
hypothesis.direction: long or flat; spot; no leverage; no shorting
hypothesis.bar: daily 00:00-24:00 UTC from six complete H4 bars built from M5; decision at the daily close; the position earns the NEXT day's close-to-close return
hypothesis.implementation: research/phase2_1/hypotheses.py functions h1_tsmom, daily_from_h4, evaluate, imported unchanged

costs.applied: per unit of absolute change in exposure
costs.basis: Binance VIP 0 published spot fee; spread/slippage allowance far above the measured ~0.001 bp

primary_test.name: timing skill, circular-shift permutation
primary_test.definition: exposure series over the validation segment is circularly shifted against next-day returns; 2000 shifts drawn uniformly from [30, n-30) with numpy default_rng(seed=0); statistic = mean daily (exposure x return) before costs; p = (count(null >= actual) + 1) / (2000 + 1); one-sided
primary_test.note: The Phase 2.1 JSON worded the statistic as 'net'; the executed code and the report used the pre-cost mean (costs are identical under a shift apart from the wrap-around point). This study freezes the statistic exactly as executed in Phase 2.1.

gates.holdout: read ONLY if validation passes; once; recorded in the dataset ledger; PASS requires net Sharpe > 0 AND net total return > 0
gates.decision: validation FAIL => H1 is stopped and the hold-out stays sealed. PASS at both stages => 'confirmed on unread data', which is a research finding, not approval to trade.

reported_metrics_non_gating: round-trip trades: count, win rate, mean and median net return, mean holding days, best, worst (descriptive; a position open at a segment boundary is marked there)
annualised net return and volatility (365 days)
t-statistic of mean net daily return
buy-and-hold total return, Sharpe and max drawdown over the same days
net return and Sharpe minus buy-and-hold
null distribution mean of the timing test
cost stress: net return and Sharpe at 2x and 3x costs
95% interval of net Sharpe from a circular block bootstrap (30-day blocks, 2000 resamples, seed 0)
known_limits_stated_before_results: 677 validation days are one market regime; the test has limited power, so FAIL does not prove absence of an effect and PASS is one confirmation, not proof
the timing test controls for average exposure, not for regime luck shared by all trend rules
signal-level daily simulation at the close; it is not run through the platform's paper engine and says nothing about execution parity (kept open as a separate engineering task)
the researcher knows the public BTC price path of 2023-2025 in aggregate
not_allowed: changing the rule, lookback, costs, test or gates after seeing any validation result
testing H2, H3 or any variant as a substitute if H1 fails
reading the hold-out after a validation fail
enabling any trading on the basis of this study
